slices.title: Bash guard judges command lines: heredoc stripping, one-line push match, tests, rules row

questions.question: Which commands count as feeding a heredoc to a shell or interpreter?
questions.chosen: Anything that is not cat or tee with a redirect keeps its heredoc scanned; only the file-writing shape is stripped, so an unknown command fails safe.

questions.question: Does a tee without a file argument count as writing to a file?
questions.chosen: No; tee must name a file, and cat must redirect to a file, otherwise the body stays in the text.

questions.question: Does C-3 (the push deny pattern and the push rule match within one line) stay in the goal after six attempts?
questions.chosen: No. C-3 is cut; the push deny pattern and the push rule go back to the whole-text match, so a push followed by prose on a later line stays a known false positive. Each adversarial round found another shell mechanism carrying words across a newline into a push: open expansions and quotes (a4-r1), an unquoted heredoc rebuilt by xargs (a4-r2), git and push split across heredoc lines (a5), a global option value touching << (a6). The heredoc half (C-1, C-2) with tests (C-4) and the rules row (C-5) lands by hand on goal/G-3 as a pull request; the goal stays in awaiting_human.
